source.title: Heterogeneous-Branch Collaborative Learning for Dialogue Generation
source.authors: Yiwei Li; Shaoxiong Feng; Bin Sun; Kan Li

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures Euclidean distances between collaborative-learning branches, a different method and setting from the original work, to assess branch representation diversity.
record.gate_note: Table 6 reports averaged inter-branch L2 distances at convergence, which bear on whether training setup affects representation similarity. The paper's response-quality metrics and cited findings from other work do not measure the claim's representation convergence.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its one representation measure (Table 6) is an averaged L2 distance between branches of collaborative-learning frameworks. Every framework couples the branches on purpose: mutual or positive distillation pulls them together, and CDL's negative distillation and attribute subsets push them apart. No independently trained models or seeds are compared, and there is no independent-training baseline, scale sweep, similarity-measure comparison or cross-model mapping. The convergence finding (Li et al. 2016c, an original source) is only cited to motivate the branch-homogeneity problem.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that attribute-aware branch training plus dual (positive and negative) distillation, with orthogonal projection, reduces branch homogenization. They also conclude it improves dialogue response quality over prior collaborative learning methods on DailyDialog and OpenSubtitles. The diversity claim rests on a single L2 table without uncertainty.
record.recipe_differences: This is a collaborative dialogue-generation study measuring inter-branch Euclidean distance, not an implementation of the original cross-model convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported inter-branch distance differs across collaborative-learning methods; CDL reports the largest value.

fits_no_version.finding: In 3-branch collaborative dialogue models on DailyDialog, branches trained on attribute-specific subsets with negative distillation have a larger averaged inter-branch L2 distance (0.308) than branches under standard collaborative distillation (0.141 to 0.198).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objective and data subsets, including explicit negative distillation, change how similar jointly trained network branches' representations become.

record.problems: The representation-diversity evidence is one averaged L2 metric at convergence. The text gives no uncertainty or reference scale for interpreting its magnitude, and CDL changes multiple training elements rather than isolating their contributions.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no cross-architecture, objective or data comparison.
No independently initialized networks. All branches are coupled by distillation or shared layers.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
Only one metric (L2), with no comparison of metrics or inputs.

No measurement of how complete alignment is, or of plateaus or causes, for independently trained models. Distances are reported only for deliberately coupled or decoupled branches, without a reference scale.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'supports V7' label is removed. The distances come from frameworks that impose similarity or dissimilarity through their training losses, so they are neither natural convergence nor evidence about what causes it. The text is study data only, and no instructions were found in it.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption representations or vision-language comparison.
The measured branches are collaboratively trained with attribute-related data and distillation; the paper does not test independently initialized networks learning shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits are examined.
No comparison of similarity measures, settings, or input distributions.
The study does not test a plateau, scale dependence, or whether a common model of reality explains alignment; it does not isolate the contributions of data selection and distillation.

rows.subject: CDL
rows.size_stated: Small Transformer branches; 2 encoder and decoder layers, 4 attention heads, 1024 feed-forward units, hidden size 256
rows.operation_detail: Averaged Euclidean (L2) distance between branches at convergence

conditions.value: attribute-aware collaborative learning with dual distillation

rows.note: The authors say this distance is significantly greater than those of the other methods and indicates that branch homogenization is greatly relieved. The paper does not provide a reference range for interpreting the magnitude.
rows.check: CDL's distance results from deliberately induced divergence (attribute subsets plus negative distillation). This is the study's own method compared with others, not convergence arising naturally, and there is no independent-training baseline or reference scale.

rows.subject: DML
rows.operation_detail: Averaged Euclidean (L2) distance between branches at convergence
rows.note: The paper compares this value with CDL and the other collaborative-learning methods.
rows.check: DML branches are trained with mutual distillation, so any similarity is induced by the training objective. No independently trained baseline is given, so the value cannot bear on V3 or V7.

rows.note: The paper compares this value with CDL and the other collaborative-learning methods.
rows.check: CL-ILR shares bottom layers and distills among branches, so similarity is induced. It is a comparator to the study's method, not a convergence test.
